## 01 · Folder, environment and readiness / โฟลเดอร์ environment และความพร้อม

The workshop folder contains compose.yml for the app, database, and volume; compose.override.yml adds the local app port; Dockerfile builds the Node app; server.js, app.js, and domain.js contain the app code; public/test.html provides the API test page; .env.example is a safe starter configuration; and db/init.sql creates the initial database tables. I copied .env.example to .env and set STUDENT_ID=6788185. I kept the local password out of this report.

Docker and Compose versions:

```
Docker Client: 29.8.2
Docker Server: 29.8.2 (Docker Desktop 4.95.0)
Docker context: desktop-linux
Docker Compose: v5.6.0
```

Evidence and explanation / หลักฐานและคำอธิบาย:

## ![](data:image/png;base64,)

I ran docker compose config --quiet; it passed. docker compose config --services listed db and app. These commands check the resolved Compose configuration; they do not start containers. Compose uses .env to substitute values in the YAML, such as the project name and database settings. A value is passed into a container only when it is listed under that service's environment: section. The password is a disposable local demo value and is not included here.

## 02 · Compose keys and startup / Key และการเริ่มระบบ

The Compose file defines two services: app and db. build: . builds the app image using the current workshop folder as its build context. image selects the PostgreSQL image. The override maps the laptop's 127.0.0.1:8085 to app port 3000. environment passes the app's port and PostgreSQL connection settings into the containers. depends_on waits for the database health check before starting the app. The app health check calls /health, which checks the database, and the database health check uses pg_isready. volumes stores the database files and mounts the initial SQL file.

I ran these commands from gacha-workshop/gacha-workshop:

```
docker compose config --quiet
docker compose config --services
docker compose up -d --build --wait
docker compose ps
docker compose logs --tail 30 app db
Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:8085/health
```

Evidence and explanation / หลักฐานและคำอธิบาย:

## ![](data:image/png;base64,)

Both app and db started healthy. The health response was:

```
{"status":"ok","database":"connected","app":"gacha"}
```

I also checked it directly in PowerShell:

```
Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:8085/health
```

PowerShell displayed status: ok, database: connected, and app: gacha.

## 03 · API and basic SQL / API และ SQL พื้นฐาน

I used student ID 6788185. The wallet started at 0 coins and 0 gems. I checked Health and Catalog, then made one recharge, one exchange, and one draw:

1. Recharged 1000 virtual coins. The wallet had 1000 coins and 0 gems.
2. Exchanged 1000 coins for 10 gems. The wallet had 0 coins and 10 gems.
3. Drew once. The wallet had 0 coins and 0 gems.
4. Read the saved history.

The PowerShell POST requests returned successful JSON responses. The API's successful write status is HTTP 201. The saved transactions were:

| Transaction ID | Type     | Coin change | Gem change |
| -------------- | -------- | ----------- | ---------- |
| 1              | recharge | +1000       | 0          |
| 2              | exchange | \-1000      | +10        |
| 3              | draw     | 0           | \-10       |

The actual draw was:

| Draw ID | Result   | Rarity | Created at (UTC)         |
| ------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------------ |
| 1       | Wind Fox | COMMON | 2026-11-05T13:37:28.394Z |

The API history returned this same draw and three transactions: recharge, exchange, and draw. The SQL result matched:

```
id | student_id | result_name | rarity | created_at
1  | 6788185    | Wind Fox    | COMMON | 2026-11-05 13:37:28.394212+00
draw_count: 1
```

The later read-only checks returned HTTP 200 for both /health and the account history route. History contained the same draw and all three transactions; I used GET only during the persistence checks.

I connected to PostgreSQL from the database container using:

```
docker compose exec -T db psql -U gacha -d gacha -c '\conninfo'
docker compose exec -T db psql -U gacha -d gacha -c '\dt'
docker compose exec -T db psql -U gacha -d gacha -c "SELECT id, student_id, result_name, rarity, created_at FROM draws WHERE student_id='6788185' ORDER BY id;"
docker compose exec -T db psql -U gacha -d gacha -c "SELECT COUNT(*) AS draw_count FROM draws WHERE student_id='6788185';"
```

Evidence and explanation / หลักฐานและคำอธิบาย:

## ![](data:image/png;base64,)

\\conninfo confirmed database gacha, user gacha, and port 5432. \\dt listed draws, transactions, and wallets. For the separate INSERT practice, I used the different ID 6788185-sql, leaving my proof wallet and draw alone:

```
INSERT INTO wallets(student_id) VALUES ('6788185-sql')
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
SELECT student_id, coins, gems FROM wallets WHERE student_id='6788185-sql';
```

The practice wallet was created with 0 coins and 0 gems.

The chance of an SSR/legendary result is 2% for each independent draw. There are five possible SSR results, each with a 0.4% chance per draw. A small number of draws does not guarantee an SSR. COMMON is a valid result, so I recorded the result I actually got rather than drawing again to seek a different one.

## 04 · Persistence and bind mounts / ข้อมูลถาวรและ bind mount

I recorded the same draw before and after each lifecycle step. I did not recharge, exchange, draw, or insert another proof row during these checks.

| Stage / ช่วง            | DB container ID                                                    | Named volume           | Original draw | Result + rarity + created_at               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Initial / เริ่มต้น      | `f5275445ecfb7b5004f74a30d802c3475773d66ebabe66eaee1f805764bd0606` | `gacha-6788185_pgdata` | 1             | Wind Fox, COMMON, 2026-11-05T13:37:28.394Z |
| Restart / หลัง restart  | `f5275445ecfb7b5004f74a30d802c3475773d66ebabe66eaee1f805764bd0606` | `gacha-6788185_pgdata` | 1             | Wind Fox, COMMON, 2026-11-05T13:37:28.394Z |
| Down/up / หลังสร้างใหม่ | `c5d02639f8110f0481a4746073831c2ec8351a55580fc049db7e59feae287e4d` | `gacha-6788185_pgdata` | 1             | Wind Fox, COMMON, 2026-11-05T13:37:28.394Z |

After restart, the DB container ID stayed the same. After down/up, it changed, but the same draw was still there. The named volume kept the data. The API and database showed the same time, just in different formats.

The Compose file has two mounts:

```
pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql
./db/init.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/01-init.sql:ro
```

The first mount is the named volume that stores PostgreSQL data. The second is the read-only `db/init.sql` file from my computer. I checked the file path with `Test-Path` and confirmed both mounts with `docker inspect`.

I first ran Compose from the wrong folder, so Docker could not find the gacha app files. Running it from the gacha workshop folder fixed that. I also changed the database name after the volume was already set up. Putting the original settings back fixed the app, and the draw remained saved.

`docker compose down` removes the containers but keeps the named volume. Adding `-v` also removes the volume and its data. So the volume keeps data when containers are replaced, but it is not a backup.
